Issued at 404 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Upper low over the Upper Midwest beginning to open up...as PV tracks 
into Hudson Bay to our north, allowing cold air aloft to spill 
southward into Ontario...and 100kt upper jet across the southern US 
propels another PV maxima eastward into the central Plains; no time 
for a break out west as another strong PV punches into the PacNW 
thanks to strong Pacific flow. Dry slot swept through the region 
last evening (cold front stretching from the eastern shore of Lake 
Superior down into Lake Huron as of 5z)...shunting warmer air and 
deepest moisture (pwats around or above 1.5in) eastward, though a 
plume of moisture remains trapped beneath the 700mb low/trowal over 
the Upper MS Valley to our west. Plume of cooler air sneaking 
in...850mb temps falling below 5C attm; much cooler air to our north 
over Ontario as noted above...where 850mb temps fall into the -5C 
and colder range. North to northeast low-level trajectories across 
Ontario into the Upper Midwest suggest low-level cold advection will 
continue...and this is reflected at the surface by a cold front 
stretching from Hudson Bay toward western Lake Superior...as 1024mb 
surface high takes over the Canadian Prairie provinces. Primary blob 
of convection associated with the cold front has exited our 
area...but some additional showers have moved in in the wake of the 
first cold front as a little more moisture works in. 

Trough to our west will begin to track northeast as energy to our 
north digs down into the back of the trough again tonight into 
Friday. This should both serve to punt the bulk of the moisture 
out...but also drop much colder air into the region, which should 
kick the lake machine into gear. More energy transits the flow out 
west, with ridging into Canada to our west; high pressure will try 
to build in Friday into Saturday, but troughing will do its best to 
hold on across the Great Lakes (a taste of things to come). Upstream 
niblet will make its way into the region Saturday as additional 
northern stream energy passes by going into Sunday; the bulk of this 
system attm appears to remain to our east. Only a brief break Sunday 
night into Monday before another system crashes in from the Canadian 
Prairies, with troughing trying to hang on over our area into 
Wednesday as the upstream flow amplifies again. Attm, signals point 
toward troughing trying to settle into the eastern US for the latter 
half of the week next week, with ridging over the west/central US. 
This idea suggests warmth and high pressure over the central US.

FORECAST DETAILS...

Breezy today/tonight...Tightening pressure gradient between high 
pressure over Canada and departing low pressure will result in 
breezy north to northeast flow entering the scene later this
afternoon into tonight; this should linger into much of Friday as 
the trough ends up closing off to our southeast. Pressure gradient 
will support sustained winds in the realm of 15-20kts across the 
EUP, perhaps into the tip of the Mitt region going into the 
afternoon. North to northeast winds could channel stronger flow into 
Traverse City as well as north facing points down the coasts. Expect 
a period of 25-35kt gusts late in the day into the 
overnight...though it appears the low-level jet may attempt to wane 
in strength Thursday night and could dial back gust potential 
quicker than expected. Still, with better fetch and perhaps a slight 
bit of isallobaric influences...think there will be a period of 
gales this evening, which would most likely be on northern Lake MI, 
particularly along the NW Coast, with less certainty for Whitefish 
Bay. Have opted to follow suit with GRR and upgrade to Gale warnings 
for the Lake MI zones this afternoon through Friday morning.  

Rain transitions to lake effect showers (snow overnight?)...Showers 
to continue today with that lobe of still anomalous (though not 
quite as anomalous as what we have just seen) moisture pivoting 
back in. With the cooler air sweeting in, appears there will be a 
fairly robust low-level fgen response with the front sweeping across 
the area this afternoon; additionally, there are signals for some 
more robust fgen aloft near and north of the surface low this 
afternoon/evening as colder air floods southward on northerly flow, 
which should also enhance QPF potential, though it is possible this 
may only impact the EUP, and at that, perhaps only a portion...as it 
may remain mostly to our east. At the same time, by late afternoon, 
temps aloft should be cold enough to support overlake instability 
generation over the EUP, spreading southward with time...resulting 
in lake enhancement to ongoing synoptic-driven activity through 
Thursday night and perhaps even into Friday, particularly over the 
EUP where deeper synoptic moisture could hold on north of the closed 
low expected to develop over southern MI. This should slowly drift 
southeastward with time Frid
